classification.difficultyReason: Read intercepts and horizontal asymptotes from supplied curves, then follow each curve in the specified direction to express end behaviour. Each feature is explicitly prompted and uses the taught graph-reading method.

spec.description: Unit square grid from -5 to 5 on both axes, all nonzero integer ticks labelled, double-ended axes and supplied decreasing exponential with arrows at both ends.
spec.mathematics: y=-2^x; y-intercept -1; horizontal asymptote y=0; negative for every x.
spec.answerVisibility: The curve is a permanent given. Feature responses are answer-only.

answer.worked: The curve crosses the $y$-axis at $y=-1$, so the $y$-intercept is $(0,-1)$.
The curve approaches the $x$-axis from below. Its horizontal asymptote is $y=0$.
Moving right along the curve, $y$ decreases without bound. Thus $y\to-\infty$ as $x\to\infty$.
Moving left along the curve, $y$ approaches the horizontal asymptote from below. Thus $y\to0$ as $x\to-\infty$.

spec.description: Unit square grid from -5 to 5 on both axes, all nonzero integer ticks labelled, double-ended axes and supplied increasing exponential with arrows at both ends.
spec.answerVisibility: The curve is a permanent given. Feature responses are answer-only.

answer.worked: The curve crosses the $y$-axis at $y=4$, so the $y$-intercept is $(0,4)$.
The curve approaches the horizontal line $y=3$ from above. Its asymptote is $y=3$.
Moving right along the curve, $y$ increases without bound. Thus $y\to\infty$ as $x\to\infty$.
Moving left along the curve, $y$ approaches the horizontal asymptote from above. Thus $y\to3$ as $x\to-\infty$.
